gen-gloria-hallelujah-fs-plein: Loose, jokey scrawl up top, with strokes like bent copper pipe. Plein follows in tidy sans letters, better for a line or two than for pages of text.
gen-gloria-hallelujah-fs-recia: Gloria Hallelujah looks like bent steel rod, wobbly and cheerful, while Recia's serif letters hold a faint, sharp stroke contrast beneath it. That mix of play and authority is the pair's best trick.
gen-gloria-hallelujah-fs-spline-sans: Bouncy, copper-pipe lettering from Gloria Hallelujah leads off, with Spline Sans below in friendly, widely gapped curves of identical weight. Past a few lines, it would feel light.
gen-gloria-hallelujah-fs-synonym: Synonym keeps its sans-serif strokes as a plain stripe of constant ink. Against the scribbly, comic Gloria Hallelujah, that steadiness is the whole appeal, one loud voice and one dependable one.
gen-gloria-hallelujah-outfit: Gloria Hallelujah scrawls its headings like pen on paper, with wide, easy turns in every s. Outfit then arrives in sans-serif form, curves stopping well before they close, made for short stretches of reading.
gen-gloria-hallelujah-plus-jakarta-sans: Comic, energetic scrawl up top, bent like copper pipe. Plus Jakarta Sans sits under it, modern and monoline, good for a handful of lines.
gen-gloria-hallelujah-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk reads as geometric and hollow-reed open. Gloria Hallelujah's comic wobble makes it feel stiff and cheeky at once, a prankster beside a straight-faced friend.
gen-indie-flower-fs-neco: Indie Flower brings a hand-drawn, relaxed look, with letters knotted close like cord and no swelling in the outlines. Neco, a dignified serif, does the opposite and swells gently from hairline to stem.
gen-indie-flower-fs-plein: Relaxed, hand-drawn letters sit up top, with a thin-free, swell-free stroke and a c and s kept widely parted. Plein's clear sans-serif shapes sit beneath, best for brief copy.
gen-indie-flower-fs-synonym: Indie Flower looks hand-drawn and inviting, its letters knotted close like cord in a macramé row. Synonym's plain stripe of ink below suits only a few lines.
